⛽️Global Fuel Surge: Reality Check & Required Response🚀

Global fuel markets have entered a sharp volatility phase. Diesel prices have surged from around $88 to nearly $238 within weeks, making it the most unstable segment. 

Pakistan is directly exposed because imports are linked to Dubai/#Oman benchmarks rather than BRENT, with #Dubai crude itself crossing $170.

📌Despite this, Pakistan’s price adjustment remains relatively contained.

• #Pakistan: ~22% increase
• #Philippines: 82%
• #Nigeria: 78%
• #UAE: 72%
• #Australia: 52%
• #UnitedStates: 41%

This reflects controlled pass-through rather than full transmission of global shocks.

Structural constraints further limit options. Russian crude is not easily compatible with Pakistan’s existing refinery configuration, most of which is older and privately operated, restricting meaningful substitution.

📌Globally, the response is not limited to subsidies. Countries are actively managing demand through direct controls and behavioral restrictions:

• #Bangladesh: reduced work week and rationing
• #SriLanka: fuel quota system via QR control
• #Myanmar: partial remote work mandates
• #Philippines: national emergency measures for distribution control

Pakistan has maintained supply stability with no panic buying, hoarding or distribution breakdown. 

However, consumption has not declined despite higher prices, indicating that price signals alone are not sufficient to reduce demand.

📌A structured SMART LOCKDOWN approach is now necessary:

– Markets: close by 9 pm
– Restaurants: close by 11 pm
– Education sector: Online
– Government: shift non essential functions to remote work

If subsidy pressure persists, provinces must align on demand-control measures.

This is the only realistic path controlled prices, targeted subsidies & strict demand management. Anything less will prolong the crisis.
